Hello, Dr. Lee. I... well, I'm here because things at work have gotten completely out of hand with the whispering and the talking. I'm the chief executive of my company, so, you know, I expect a certain level of office politics and chatter, but this is... it's beyond that now. I keep hearing people talking about me. And... I suppose, looking at it objectively, he's right. I mean, I barely speak to him anymore. I come home, I put my bag down, and I just sit there in the living room. I don't have the energy to ask about his day, and I certainly don't have the desire to talk about mine. 

And it's not just at home with him, it's at the office, too. Which is honestly the hardest part for me to admit, because my business is my life. Or, at least, it used to be. I used to be the person driving every single idea. I was the absolute engine of that company. If we had a new product launch or a promotional opening, I was the one working the room, calling people the very next morning, following up on every single lead, pushing my team to be better, faster, sharper. I loved it. I absolutely lived for that thrill. 

But now... I don't know. It's like someone just unplugged me from the wall. Lately, I can go into my office, shut the door, and just sit at my desk for hours. Literally hours. My assistant will print out the daily agenda and place it right in front of me, right on my desk blotter, and I will just stare at it. I won't read it. I won't action anything on it. I just stare at the bullet points until the letters don't even look like real words anymore. I barely speak to my staff at all now—I've been communicating almost entirely through very brief emails, if I communicate at all, because I just can't bring myself to actually open my mouth and have a conversation with them. 

It's the strangest, most unsettling feeling, Doctor, because I look at this company I built from nothing, this work that I used to love so much that it was practically my entire identity, and I feel almost nothing. No excitement, no pride, no urgency. Just this heavy, flat blankness. I sit there staring at the agenda, knowing intellectually that I should care, knowing I should be calling our suppliers or rallying the marketing team, but I just... don't. It's like the part of me that felt anything at all for this business has just completely evaporated.

No, I don't think so. I mean, you asked about feeling worthless or guilty, and... no. Why would I feel guilty? I built a multimillion-dollar enterprise from the ground up. I don't feel worthless, either. I know exactly what my worth is. The board knows my worth, too, which is exactly why they spend so much time whispering and plotting to get around me. I know I'm valuable, I just... I don't feel connected to that value anymore. But no, no guilt. I haven't done anything wrong to feel guilty about. I've given my entire adult life to that company. 

And as for my appetite, no, that hasn't changed at all. Like I mentioned, my husband makes that incredible roasted salmon on Sundays—we get it from this specific fishmonger downtown, always wild-caught, and he does this wonderful dill and lemon glaze—and I still eat that. I eat my catered lunches at the office, too. Usually it's just a Caesar salad with grilled chicken, very standard, very predictable, but I eat it. My clothes all fit exactly the same, too. I get all my work suits custom-tailored, so I would absolutely notice if I had lost or gained even a few pounds. The seamstress I use is incredibly precise, she measures down to the quarter-inch, so no, my weight is perfectly stable. 

You mentioned concentration, too, and... well, like I said a few minutes ago, I do just sit and stare at my daily agenda until the bullet points don't look like real words anymore. But it's not that my brain is broken or that I *can't* concentrate if there was an actual fire to put out. It's just that I don't have the drive to even try to focus on it. It's a total lack of caring, not a lack of cognitive ability. If I actually cared, I could focus just fine.
